Definition: from G1937; a longing (especially for what is forbidden):--concupiscence, desire, lust (after).
BiblicalUsage: Epithymía is desire — a longing, especially for what is forbidden. The lust of the flesh, the lust of the eyes, and the pride of life are all of this world, John says, and they do not come from the Father. Paul traces sin's work through it: where there is no law, desire has no handle, but the commandment wakes it up.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe epithymía is the word for the wanting that rules us before Christ rules us. I hold that the answer is not to pretend the wanting is gone, but to walk in the Spirit, so the desire no longer gets its way.
